newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian tin and nickel up on import duty fears.
newsitem.headline: Indian tin and nickel up on import duty fears.

text.p: Tin and nickel prices jumped up on the local market on Thursday, dealers said, but other base metals were steady in a narrow range amid limited activity.
Tin and nickel prices were driven by rumours that the Indian government had hiked import duty on these metals by 10 percent, said Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metals Exchange.
"However we have so far not received any confirmation for this rumour from the Indian government," he said.
Meanwhile nickel prices in the Bombay market rose today by 300 rupees at 37,200 rupees per quintal while tin prices lifted by 200 rupees at 31,400 rupees per quintal.
"If no confirmation is received from the Indian government regarding duty hike shortly then market may come down again," Parikh said.
Other base metals were steady in dull activity because few traders turned up as banks were closed to observe the birth anniversary of Lord Buddha.

Copper was quiet at 13,600 rupees per quintal, as was zinc at 7,950 rupees and lead at 4,150 rupees per quintal. Aluminium was indicated at the previous level of 7,600 rupees per quintal but activity was nominal
